relaxation.pulseHint: Apply a pulse to tip the magnetization

common.mainFieldHelp: Field of the main magnet in tesla. The energy gap between the two spin states grows with it.
common.powerHelp: Sets how many radio-wave photons the source sends up through the sample each second.
common.frequencyHelp: Frequency of the radio waves in megahertz. Nuclei absorb only near their resonance frequency.
common.radioViewHelp: Show the radio waves as a continuous wave or as individual photons.
common.nucleusHelp: Choose which kind of nucleus fills the sample. Each has its own gyromagnetic ratio.
common.resonanceReached: On resonance: the radio frequency matches the energy gap, so nuclei absorb.

screenSummary.playArea: Twenty atomic nuclei sit in a sample chamber between the coils of a large magnet. Each nucleus points either along the magnetic field, its lower-energy state, or against it, its higher-energy state. A radio-wave source below the chamber sends radio waves up through the sample. An energy-level diagram shows how many nuclei are in each state.
screenSummary.controlArea: Controls set the main magnetic field, the sample nucleus, the radio-wave power and frequency, how the radio waves are drawn, and whether field arrows and precession are shown. Time controls pause and step the simulation, and Reset All starts over.
screenSummary.interactionHint: Turn up the power, then change the frequency or the field until the nuclei start to flip.

nmr.currentDetailsPattern: Field {{field}} tesla. Radio waves at {{frequency}} megahertz, power {{power}} percent. {{aligned}} of {{total}} nuclei are aligned with the field. {{resonance}}
nmr.offResonance: The source is not on resonance.

screenSummary.playArea: A head full of hydrogen nuclei lies between the coils of a large magnet, with gradient coils below and to the left. A radio-wave source sends radio waves up through the head. Nuclei that absorb flip, and when they relax they emit radio waves toward a detector on the right.
screenSummary.controlArea: Controls set the main field, the horizontal and vertical gradients, the radio-wave power and frequency, and what is shown. A button adds or removes a tumor. Time controls pause and step the simulation, and Reset All starts over.
screenSummary.interactionHint: Turn on a gradient so the resonance frequency changes across the head, then tune the frequency to pick out one slice.

mri.currentDetailsPattern: Field {{field}} tesla, horizontal gradient {{horizontal}} tesla, vertical gradient {{vertical}} tesla. Radio waves at {{frequency}} megahertz, power {{power}} percent. The detector receives {{count}} photons per second. {{tumor}}
mri.gradientHelp: Difference in field between the two edges of the chamber, in tesla. A gradient makes the resonance frequency depend on position.
mri.tumorButtonHelp: Adds or removes a tumor, a region of densely packed nuclei.

screenSummary.playArea: A sphere shows the net magnetization of a tissue's protons as a red arrow, with the main field pointing up. An RF pulse tips the arrow away from the field; it then precesses around the field while its upward part recovers and its sideways part decays. Two graphs record the longitudinal and transverse magnetization since the last pulse.
screenSummary.controlArea: Controls choose a tissue or set T1 and T2 directly, set the flip angle, apply a pulse or return to equilibrium, and choose what is shown. Time controls set the speed, pause and step, and Reset All starts over.
screenSummary.interactionHint: Apply a 90 degree pulse and watch the two kinds of relaxation, then compare tissues.

relaxation.currentDetailsPattern: {{tissue}}: T1 {{t1}} milliseconds, T2 {{t2}} milliseconds. Longitudinal magnetization {{mz}}, transverse magnetization {{mxy}}.
relaxation.tissueHelp: Choose a tissue to load its typical T1 and T2 at 1.5 tesla.
relaxation.t1Help: Time for the magnetization along the field to recover most of the way, in milliseconds.
relaxation.t2Help: Time for the sideways magnetization, and the signal, to decay, in milliseconds. Never longer than T1.
relaxation.flipAngleHelp: How far the pulse tips the magnetization away from the field, in degrees.
relaxation.applyPulseHelp: Tips the magnetization by the flip angle and restarts the graphs.
relaxation.equilibriumHelp: Puts the magnetization back along the field and clears the graphs.
relaxation.rotatingFrameHelp: View from a frame turning with the precession, so the arrow stops circling.

preferences.title: Simulation
preferences.snapToResonanceDescription: Releasing the field or frequency slider close to resonance moves it exactly onto resonance, as in PhET's original.
